claims.summary: For the Tate Kronecker kernel K_Q with Q not a period and y(s)=(2+s)/(2-s), the coefficient E_j(x)=[v^(j-1)] K_Q(x/y(v))/(1-v^2/4) has automorphy Q^(-1), poles only on the period orbit, and pure local principal part E_j(y(s))=s^(-j)+O(1), for every j>=1 in characteristic different from two.
claims.assessment: Working proof by the exact Cauchy identity 1/((y(s)/y(v)-1)(1-v^2/4))=1/(s-v)-1/(2-v). No factorial is inverted, so the formula extends past the characteristic. The first three depths recover the previous intrinsic merged construction.
claims.rationale: Supplies explicit pure principal parts for the six-level dimension-six matrix; an extension of the existing theta basis for this route, without a separate novelty claim.
claims.next_action: Use the pure principal columns to analyze the exact constant cross-scale determinant coefficient.

claims.summary: For every d>=4 in characteristic different from two, the dimension-six paired space has four explicit top-pole conditions, eight Fourier Hasse-jet conditions on the first branch coset and twelve on the second. On a non-torsion marked Tate curve, pure-principal kernels and inverse local G jets give every column of its exact 20-by-20 marked matrix. Its invertibility is equivalent to paired-limit normality; no all-degree nonvanishing is asserted.
claims.assessment: Working proof from the polynomial multiplicity table, translation characters, inertia parity and explicit triangular principal-part inversion. The exact smallest bulk control d=4,p=3 has a nonzero normalized coefficient at t^48; constant and full cross-scale matrices agree through t^67 at the sampled mark. This is an encoding and leading-term control, not a uniform theorem.
claims.rationale: Removes the previously uncomputed basis conversion and specifies the actual coupled determinant, preserving small-characteristic Hasse conditions. The remaining implication is its uniform nonvanishing.
claims.next_action: Prove a uniform formula for the constant cross-scale leading coefficient and bound corrections; classify and repair any exceptional degree/prime families.
